small_guidance:
- The conv (Conv3d 3→16, 16×30×30×14 outputs) almost certainly dominates the 0.844 ms; the fused norm/clamp/max kernel is already cheap. Add autotune configs with smaller BLOCK_S (128, 256) and num_warps=2 since S=14×30×30=12600 and C=16 — current 512–2048 wastes warps on the second (max-reduce) pass.
- Cache `x*mult` in registers across the two passes by sizing BLOCK_S so the whole row [C=16, S] fits (S=12600 → too big), or keep stats in pass 1 and only re-multiply once in pass 2 by storing x_raw·mult into a scratch tensor — but actually better: precompute mean/var with a tiny separate kernel and skip the redundant pass-1 multiply.
- Pre-fold the conv bias and the first multiplier into a single (weight·m, bias·m) so instance-norm input is produced directly scaled; this removes one broadcast multiply per element in the fused kernel.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit gather over the 3×3×3×IC=81 K-dim. With OC=16 and IC=3, K is tiny — use BLOCK_M=16 (full OC), BLOCK_N=64–128 spatial, BLOCK_K=81 fully unrolled. Fuse the conv bias add, the per-channel multiplier, and even a partial reduction directly into the epilogue.
- Fuse conv + multiplier + instance-norm + clamp + multiplier + max-over-C into a two-stage pipeline: stage 1 computes conv outputs streaming and accumulates per-(N,C) sum/sum² in a small [N,C] scratch (C=16 fits in registers); stage 2 re-runs conv (or reads cached output) to apply normalization, clamp, scale, and reduce over C in-register, writing [N,S] directly. Keeps S=12600 elements off-chip only once.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout end-to-end so the C=16 max-reduction is along the contiguous axis and a single program can hold all 16 channels in registers while striding over spatial tiles.
